evidence_summary.notes: Single-source convergence intake (MAP-Elites / Quality-Diversity, Cully et al. 2015) on the committed-action-diversity conversion ceiling. Primary sources are peer-reviewed/archival; intake is partial pending algorithm-level extraction of the archive-insertion + per-niche replacement rule and the outer-loop-vs-inner-loop scope reconciliation. The candidate claim is registered candidate/substrate_conditional/generation v3 and promotes nothing on its own.

falsification.claim_under_test: Committed-action diversity should be preserved through the selection/commit step by an explicit behavioral-descriptor-indexed ARCHIVE of per-niche elites (MECH-442, MAP-Elites analog) -- generalizing the validated V3-EXQ-569i top-k shortlist (the descriptor-free degenerate archive) -- rather than collapsing to F's single global optimum at the bare E3 argmin (MECH-439 F-dominance).
could_be_wrong_if: A behavioral-descriptor-indexed committed-selection archive does NOT lift committed-action-class entropy strict-above BOTH collapsed-proposer and matched-noise on >=2/3 seeds beyond what the descriptor-free top-k shortlist (V3-EXQ-569i) already achieves -- the archive earns no keep over the simpler top-k.

The archive lifts committed diversity only by selecting F-dominated / clearly-worse (unsafe) actions whose F-cost exceeds the per-niche-elite bound -- a quality/safety regression, falsifying the safety-preserving framing.

The conversion ceiling turns out to be driven entirely by F's variance share rather than the selection structure, in which case rebalancing F's E3 variance share directly (MECH-439) is the right fix and no archive structure helps.
falsification.notes: Falsifier is pre-registered per the candidate claim; the V3-EXQ-569i top-k PASS supplies the baseline the archive must beat, and the V3-EXQ-571 F-variance-share metric is the instrumentation a future 2x2 (F-de-collapse) x (archive vs top-k) ablation would reuse.

deltas.title: Behavioral-descriptor committed-selection archive (MECH-442, MAP-Elites analog)
deltas.proposal: Register a candidate REE claim that committed-action diversity survives the selection/commit step via an explicit behavioral-descriptor-indexed archive of per-niche elites -- partition the E3 candidate set by a behavioral descriptor (first-action / committed-action class / e2.world_forward strategy signature), retain the F-best candidate per niche, commit by a coverage-aware rule -- generalizing the validated V3-EXQ-569i top-k shortlist.
deltas.rationale: MAP-Elites per-niche elite retention is the working external instance of diversity-survives-selection; REE's commit collapses to F's global optimum (MECH-439 F-dominance) and the only existing converter is the thin top-k near-tie shortlist.

deltas.title: Coverage-objective committed-selection-niche calibration (folded into MECH-442)
deltas.proposal: Register (as a MECH-442 note) that the committed-selection-niche calibration -- which behavioral axis defines a niche; how many F-best-per-niche elites the commit draws from -- should derive from a coverage/diversity objective rather than a single hand-set top-k k; the 569i k=3 is the degenerate single-axis (F-rank) version.
deltas.rationale: QD shows descriptor design + archive resolution, not a fixed k, governs how much diversity survives selection.

decisions.notes: Recommended outcome hybridize: combine REE's existing committed-selection converter (the validated V3-EXQ-569i top-k shortlist) with the MAP-Elites behavioral-descriptor archive structure -- i.e. register MECH-442 as a candidate AMENDING the GAP-B conversion locus (generalizing the descriptor-free top-k into a behavioral-descriptor-indexed per-niche-elite archive), NOT a parallel module. Final outcome and any decide-to-build set during REE_assembly governance adjudication; the candidate claim is registered candidate/substrate_conditional/generation v3 and promotes nothing.
